steps_raw.instruction: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX)

Scope and Applicability: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX) is used for applications including tissue bath solution during electrophysiological recording for probing synaptic connections under physiological conditions.
Calcium Chloride, dihydrate (CaCl2·2 H2O) (Sigma C3881, Sigma C3306 or equivalent)
D-Glucose (C6H12O6; aka Dextrose) (Sigma G7021 or equivalent)
Magnesium Sulfate, Heptahydrate (MgSO4·7 H2O) (Sigma M1880 or equivalent)
Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH2PO4 • H2O) (Sigma S9638 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (KCl) (Sigma P9333, Sigma P5405 or equivalent)
Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3) (Sigma S5761 or equivalent)
Sodium Chloride (NaCl) (JT Baker 4058 purchased as VWR JT4058 or equivalent)
Sodium L-Ascorbate (Sigma A4034 or equivalent)
Filter system, 0.45 µm (VWR 28199-976 or equivalent)
Disposable plastic spatulas
Osmometer (Vapro 5560 or equivalent)
Magnetic stir bar remover or additional stir bar
1L or 2L volumetric flask
1L or 2L polystyrene bottle
1L or 2L liter of Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX), pH 7.3, Osmolarity 285-305 mOsm containing:
1.3 mM/2 mM Calcium Chloride, dihydrate
ACSF.IX may contain 1.3 mM or 2.0 mM Calcium Chloride, dehydrate depending on experimental conditions (Table 1).
1mM /2mM Magnesium Sulfate, Heptahydrate
If ACSF.IX contains 1.3 mM Calcium Chloride use 1 mM Magnesium Sulfate
If ACSF.IX contains 2.0 mM Calcium Chloride use 2.0 mM Magnesium Sulfate (Table 1).
1.25 mM Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate
3 mM Potassium Chloride
25 mM Sodium Bicarbonate
126 mM Sodium Chloride
0.16mM Sodium L-Ascorbate
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Label a clean 1 or 2 liter polystyrene bottle with the reagent name, date and preparer’s initials.
Obtain a stir bar and rinse it thoroughly with MilliQ water before placing in a clean and labeled 1 or 2 liter beaker.
Methodology/Procedures: (record all lot numbers and volumes used in the appropriate reagent prep notebook):
ACSF.IX has a shelf life of one week, stored at 4°C.
Determine the volume of ACSF to prepare. Table 1 lists the reagent quantities required to make either 1L or 2L of ACSF.IX.
To make 1L or 2L of Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX):
Using a graduated cylinder, measure 1500 ml of MilliQ Water. Add the water to the previously labeled beaker.
Place the container on a stir plate and begin stirring at a medium setting (400 RPM or higher).
Table 1: Reagents required for preparation of 1L or 2L of ACSF.IX
Add reagents in order (top to bottom) as described in Table 1.
Use either 1.0 mM magnesium sulfate and 1.3 mM calcium chloride OR 2.0 mM magnesium sulfate and 2.0 mM calcium chloride depending on experimental conditions.
Note: Allow sufficient time for magnesium sulfate to dissolve before adding calcium chloride to avoid precipitation of divalent ions.
Allow all reagents to fully dissolve into solution before proceeding.
Adjust final volume to 2 L with MilliQ Water using a volumetric flask.
Measure and record the osmolarity of a 10 µl sample of the solution using an osmometer.
If the osmolarity is not 285-305 mOsm (285-305 mmol/kg), discard and remake solution.
Record the date of preparation, lot numbers of all components and osmolarity.
Dispose of excess reagents directly into municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with MilliQ Water.

Rinse all beakers, graduated cylinders, and other equipment used to prepare ACSF solutions with MilliQ Water only (No Detergent). Invert all beakers and graduated cylinders and leave on clean absorbent pad to air dry.
Technical Information:
Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX) has a shelf life of one week, stored at 4°C.
Use within one week from the day it is made, or at the discretion of the investigator.
